title: Active-versus-passive sensory coding
disposition_reason: The unchanged 92-row velocity scorer is joined by complete numerical observation/collection, an SVG/numeric typed operator API and submitted-programme source. These preserve 141 active training trials, 40 passive primary queries and 52 active secondary queries. Actual provider delivery, image-only perception, Linux runtime and scientific method qualification remain open; kinematic matching and causal sensory-coding claims remain unestablished.

scientific_target.question: How well does a decoder trained only on active reaches reconstruct nominal velocity on passive perturbations, and how does its transfer loss compare with same-information direction controls and a separately calibrated passive decoder?
scientific_target.known_answer: Two measured nominal velocity components in m/s per query, at the declared retrospective 120 msmovement-onset target.
scientific_target.answer_origin: Area 2_Bump Han 2017-12-07 behavioral measurements in the fixed 92 query packet.
scientific_target.case_unit: One trial-level two-component nominal velocity response, not the 30-bin trajectory of 021.
scientific_target.independent_unit: One Han macaque/session;40 passive primary and 52 active secondary trials.
scientific_target.inference_scope: Exposed within-session active-to-passive predictive transfer. Passive-trained comparison is privileged calibration; a difference does not isolate mechanism or prove matching of behavioral state.
exclusions: A candidate score is the fixed-reference active-minus-passive diagnostic.
Direction strata alone establish kinematic matching.
Causal sensory coding, online prediction, new-animal generalization or native-understanding performance.
